roadmap_thesis: Build bookkeeping competence from scratch through a fictional shop's escalating transactions, moving from account classification to journal entries, ledgers, trial balance, and basic financial statements, all practiced in-app with numeric answers and written reasoning.
anti_goals: No real accounting software or real money; the learner has no business, so all practice uses supplied fictional shop cases.
Avoid premature tax or regulatory topics; they require foundations this cycle does not build.
Skip memorizing accounting standards; basic double-entry mechanics come first for a true beginner.
Do not outsource exercises to external spreadsheets or paper; all work stays in-app with provided data.

items.title: Classify fictional shop accounts by type: in-app course and 12-transaction worksheet
items.description: Complete an in-app lesson sequence introducing the accounting equation (Assets = Liabilities + Equity) and the definitions of asset, liability, and equity accounts, followed by a worked example where the owner invests cash into the fictional shop so the learner sees the entry on both sides of the equation. Then work through twelve escalating fictional shop transactions — such as owner cash investment, buying display shelves, taking a small bank loan, and purchasing inventory on credit — classifying each as asset, liability, or equity with a one-sentence written justification. A brief diagnostic at the start checks prerequisite arithmetic and the meaning of debit and credit sides, and targeted review is provided if needed. The lesson supplies all fictional data, worked examples, feedback, and a revision round after incorrect answers. This fits a true beginner because every concept is anchored to one concrete fictional shop rather than abstract definitions. Quality check: at least 11 of 12 correct on the final in-app attempt.
items.success_metric: At least 11 of 12 fictional shop transactions correctly classified as asset, liability, or equity in the final in-app worksheet attempt.

meta_json.primary_mission: Learn the accounting equation and the five core account categories, then classify at least twelve fictional shop transactions into asset, liability, or equity accounts with written reasoning, producing a completed in-app classification worksheet that becomes the foundation for journal entries in week two.
meta_json.predicted_friction: As a complete beginner, the learner will confuse equity with assets when the fictional owner invests cash into the shop, seeing 'money in the business' and labeling it an asset only; prerequisites for debit/credit mechanics are also not yet established.
meta_json.friction_solution: Anchor every classification to the worked example where the owner's cash investment appears on both sides of the equation — cash (asset) up and owner's equity up — and include that exact case in the daily flash drill with immediate feedback. Add a brief in-app diagnostic before the worksheet and targeted review cards on equation structure, without claiming debit/credit mechanics are mastered this week.

items.title: Daily account-type flash classification drill: five sets of eight items
items.description: Run a five-day daily rhythm of short classification drills inside the CMPYS lesson. Each session presents eight quick fictional shop items — for example, 'cash register,' 'amount owed to a supplier,' 'owner's original investment' — drawn from a rotating item bank that deliberately mixes in the classic confuser: the owner investing cash, which increases an asset and equity simultaneously. Learners answer in-app by selecting the account type and writing a one-line justification for any item they miss. Session duration is about 10 minutes, keeping total weekly time near one hour. Recorded evidence is the in-app streak of completed sets plus short written explanations for missed items, which feed week two's journal-entry work. This cadence builds automatic classification, which is the raw material for journal entries.
items.success_metric: Five consecutive daily short sets of eight classification items each answered in-app, with a written explanation recorded for every missed item.

meta_json.predicted_friction: As a complete beginner, the learner will confuse equity with assets when the fictional owner invests cash into the shop, seeing 'money in the business' and labeling it an asset only; prerequisites for debit/credit mechanics are also not yet established.
meta_json.friction_solution: Anchor every classification to the worked example where the owner's cash investment appears on both sides of the equation — cash (asset) up and owner's equity up — and include that exact case in the daily flash drill with immediate feedback. Add a brief in-app diagnostic before the worksheet and targeted review cards on equation structure, without claiming debit/credit mechanics are mastered this week.
meta_json.daily_instructions: Each day for five days, open the Today screen and start the flash classification set of eight items. Set a 10-minute timer. For each item, read the fictional shop description, choose asset, liability, or equity, and move on without second-guessing. When the timer ends or all eight are answered, review the feedback: for every incorrect item, write one sentence in the app explaining why the correct type applies, using the accounting equation as the anchor. If the same account type is missed twice across days, re-read that category's worked example before ending the session. Expected output: one completed eight-item set with recorded answers and explanations for misses. Stop when the set is finished or the timer hits 10 minutes, whichever comes first — no extra sets.
